skill.name: rust-2024-migration

content.value_statement: Rust migrations can be hard when new edition features change style and compiler expectations. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code identify Rust 2024 refactoring opportunities and migration steps.
actual_capabilities: Identifies nested if-let and match patterns that can use let chains.
Suggests native async closures for manual async move closure patterns.
Explains when native async fn in traits can replace async-trait.
Notes when async-trait is still needed for dynamic dispatch.
Highlights Rust 2024 match ergonomics behavior changes.
Provides a Rust 2024 migration checklist for Cargo.toml and cargo fix.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not edit files automatically.
It does not run cargo fix, cargo check, or project tests.
Compiler version requirements must be verified for each project.
Some recommendations need project-specific review for public APIs.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Crate to Rust 2024
use_cases.description: Plan edition changes, identify likely refactors, and review minimum compiler requirements before migration.

use_cases.title: Simplify Async Rust Code
use_cases.description: Find async closures and trait patterns that can use modern Rust syntax with fewer helper crates.

use_cases.title: Review Migration Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check whether Rust 2024 refactors are appropriate, readable, and compatible with project constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Find 2024 Candidates
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan for simple modernization opportunities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust module and list patterns that could use Rust 2024 features. Focus on let chains, async closures, and match ergonomics.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Edition Upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration planning for a crate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Rust 2024 migration plan for this crate. Include Cargo.toml changes, compiler version concerns, cargo fix steps, and manual review points.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Async Traits
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of async trait usage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these async trait definitions and explain which can use native async fn in traits. Identify any cases that still require async-trait for dynamic dispatch.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Migration Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness assessment before a larger migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Rust project for Rust 2024 readiness. Prioritize risky changes, public API impact, test gaps, and refactors that should be split into separate commits.

output_examples.input: A function uses several nested option checks before returning a value.
output: The skill identifies the nested control flow as a let chain candidate.
It explains that the change requires Rust 1.88 or later and edition 2024.
It recommends keeping the original shape if the chain would reduce readability.

output_examples.input: A service trait uses async-trait for methods without dynamic dispatch.
output: The skill suggests native async functions in traits where object safety is not required.
It warns that boxed dynamic trait objects may still need async-trait.
It asks the user to confirm public API and minimum compiler support.

output_examples.input: A crate is still configured for the 2021 edition.
output: The skill outlines an edition update checklist.
It includes cargo fix, compiler version checks, and manual review of modernized patterns.
It separates mechanical migration steps from optional readability refactors.

best_practices: Verify the project minimum supported Rust version before applying each recommendation.
Separate edition migration commits from optional style refactors for easier review.
Run cargo fix, cargo check, and tests after applying Rust 2024 changes.
anti_patterns: Do not replace async-trait when dynamic dispatch still requires it.
Do not apply let chains when they make complex conditions harder to read.
Do not change the edition without checking downstream users and public API impact.

faq.question: Does this skill modify Rust files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides migration guidance and review suggestions. File edits require a separate user request.

faq.question: Which Rust edition does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Rust 2024 migration patterns, especially let chains, async closures, match ergonomics, and gen blocks.

faq.question: Can it run cargo fix for me?
faq.answer: No. The skill documentation only lists cargo fix as a migration checklist step.

faq.question: Does it remove async-trait everywhere?
faq.answer: No. It explains that async-trait can still be needed for dynamic dispatch with trait objects.

faq.question: Is compiler compatibility checked automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill reminds users to verify compiler versions for the selected Rust 2024 features.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
